$description: Design tokens for the Tribal Law Project website. Format: Design Tokens Community Group draft (https://www.designtokens.org/tr/drafts/format/). The build turns these into CSS custom properties named --<group>-<token>, for example --color-paper. Names are spelled out (docs/style-guide.md, section 7). See site/DESIGN.md for how each token is used. Palette of Nov. 21, 2026: deep teal and burnt orange, chosen by the lead author; it carries no tribal symbolism and is a placeholder until commissioned Native art can inform it.

surface-raised.$description: Hover cards and popovers, with a shadow.

control-border.$description: Borders of inputs and quiet buttons (non-text minimum 3:1). 4.7:1 on paper.

action-text.$description: Text on a primary button. 5.5:1 on action.

band.$description: Masthead band behind the site name and main menu.

band-text.$description: Text on the band. 9.6:1 on band.

band-inset.$description: The masthead's search box at rest, a recessed strip in the band (Trevor, Nov. 27, 2026, closed look 2 in design/header-search/closed-looks). Band text is 12.2:1 on it.

band-progress.$description: The filled part of a progress bar on the band, such as the Sponsorship page's goal. 4.8:1 on band.

track-alternative-dispute-resolution.$description: Section numbers and labels in the ADR track. Always paired with the words. 5.3:1 on paper.

track-peacemaking.$description: Section numbers, labels and the top rule in the peacemaking track. Always paired with the words. 5.8:1 on paper.

placeholder-background.$description: Fill-in template placeholders such as [Name of Nation]. Ink on it 14.2:1.

comment-highlight.$description: Words someone commented on, in the editor. Ink on it 14.2:1.

comment-rule.$description: Underline of commented words, and the edge of the comment being written. 5.3:1 on paper.

status-published.$description: Text of the Published label in the essay editor (essay-editor-mockups/4). 7.2:1 on its background.

status-draft.$description: Text of draft labels: draft changes, new components, DRAFT beside the line numbers. 7.5:1 on its background.

status-draft-rule.$description: Bar beside a changed or new component, and the edge of draft labels. 3.2:1 on paper.

status-draft-background.$description: Fill of the draft changes label.

status-review.$description: Text of In review labels and the In review band. 8.9:1 on its background.

status-review-rule.$description: Bar beside a section in review, and the edge of the in-review label. 6.6:1 on paper.

status-review-background.$description: Fill of the in-review label and band.

status-review-border.$description: Edge of the In review band.

danger.$description: Errors, and the button that confirms a delete. 7.8:1 on paper; white text on it is 8.1:1.

added-background.$description: Words added, on Recent changes and when comparing versions. Ink is 13.5:1 on it.

removed-background.$description: Words taken out, on Recent changes and when comparing versions. Ink is 13.1:1 on it.

art-reserved.$description: Empty space reserved for commissioned art.

map-class-0.$description: Map: no nation recorded. Tiles also print their count.

scrollbar-thumb.$description: Scrollbar thumb, the part a reader drags. 4.0:1 on the scrollbar track and 4.4:1 on paper (non-text minimum 3:1).

scrollbar-track.$description: Scrollbar track, the strip the thumb moves along. Same as surface, like the side rails.

scan-code-dark.$description: Dark squares of a QR code, the same in both themes so phone cameras can read it. 20:1 on scan-code-light.

image-backing.$description: Plate behind a nation's seal or logo. Seals are drawn for light paper, so in dark mode they sit on a light plate and their dark lines stay visible (Trevor, Nov. 23, 2026).

scan-code-light.$description: Light squares and quiet zone of a QR code, the same in both themes.

viewer-background.$description: Behind a picture opened in the image viewer, the same in both themes so every picture is seen against the same dark ground.

viewer-text.$description: Text in the image viewer. 16.2:1 on viewer-background.

viewer-text-muted.$description: Credit and secondary text in the image viewer. 10.3:1 on viewer-background.

viewer-link.$description: Links in the image viewer, always underlined. 11.0:1 on viewer-background.

viewer-control-border.$description: Borders of buttons in the image viewer (non-text minimum 3:1). 6.0:1 on viewer-background.

timeline-treaty.$description: Timeline: treaties and land. Always beside its kind's icon and name. 4.5:1 on paper. The five kinds must pass npm run check:color-vision.

timeline-document.$description: Timeline: laws and agreements. Always beside its kind's icon and name. 5.8:1 on paper. The five kinds must pass npm run check:color-vision.

timeline-case.$description: Timeline: court decisions. Always beside its kind's icon and name. 5.3:1 on paper. The five kinds must pass npm run check:color-vision.

timeline-opinion.$description: Timeline: Tribal court opinions. Always beside its kind's icon and name. 8.4:1 on paper. The five kinds must pass npm run check:color-vision.

timeline-federal.$description: Timeline: federal law. Always beside its kind's icon and name. 4.7:1 on paper. The five kinds must pass npm run check:color-vision.

reading.$description: The default for everything. Noto fonts load only for the characters Atkinson Hyperlegible Next lacks, through unicode-range. A reader can pick one of the other families in Settings; the site then points --font-family-reading at it.

atkinson-hyperlegible-next.$description: The same list as reading. It never changes, so the font dropdown in Settings can show the default font in its own typeface after a reader has picked another font.

serif.$description: Reader's choice in Settings. Noto Serif covers the letters in nation names that Atkinson Hyperlegible Next lacks, such as ʻ, ō, ʷ and ʔ.

measure.$description: The one width every block of running text, notice and panel is held to: a share of the page's column (cqi, a percentage of the nearest size container, which is <main>). 100 fills the column, the default Trevor chose on Nov. 23, 2026. Readers set it from 40 to 100 percent with the Text width slider in Settings.

side-column.$description: Widest column beside the text on wide screens, such as At a glance and its map on a nation's page.

label-column.$description: Width of the label column in a list of terms and answers (a summary list), beside the text.

field.$description: Widest a one-line text field grows: room for a long name, address or title. Fields never grow past the text width, and narrow screens make them narrower.

field-short.$description: Width of a field for a short answer: a date, a time, an amount, a code.

popover.$description: Widest a small box that opens over the page gets: menus, link previews, citation popups, the search panel, notices. Always held inside the screen.

popover-form.$description: Width of a short form that opens over the page, such as the masthead's sign-in panel (design/sign-in-popover). Always held inside the screen.

panel.$description: Widest a dialog or a box that stands alone gets, such as the sign-in box. Always held inside the screen.

card-min.$description: Narrowest a card in a grid of cards gets before the grid drops a column.

target-minimum.$description: Smallest size of a button or menu item. WCAG 2.2 requires 24 px; the project uses 44 px.

motion.$description: How long movement takes and how it speeds up and slows down (site/DESIGN.md, section 6, "Motion"). Every transition, animation and script animation on the site takes its timing from here, through src/lib/motion.ts or the --motion-* custom properties. Motion happens only in answer to something the reader does. When the reader picks Reduce motion in Settings, or the device asks for less motion, every duration becomes 0.

short.$description: Small changes in place: an arrow turning, a button's state.

medium.$description: Something appearing or moving: a citation window, a dialog, a folding section, the map gliding to a new zoom, a page change.

long.$description: Larger movements, such as chart bars moving to new values.

highlight.$description: How long the mark on a source or note a link has just gone to takes to fade to its resting color.

standard.$description: Movement within the page, starting quickly and settling gently.

enter.$description: Something appearing: it arrives quickly and slows to a stop.

exit.$description: Something leaving: it starts slowly and speeds away.
